title: Old Tax Regime: Slabs & Deductions for FY 2025-26
description: The old tax regime remains an option for taxpayers in FY 2025-26 (AY 2026-27), despite the new regime becoming the default. It allows a wide array of deductio.

faq.q: Is the old tax regime still available for FY 2025-26?
faq.a: Yes, the old tax regime is still an option for taxpayers for Financial Year 2025-26 (Assessment Year 2026-27), alongside the new tax regime.

faq.q: What is the standard deduction in the old tax regime?
faq.a: Salaried individuals can claim a standard deduction of ₹50,000 from their gross salary under the old tax regime.

faq.q: Can I switch between the old and new tax regimes every year?
faq.a: Yes, salaried individuals and those not having business income can choose between the old and new tax regimes each financial year when filing their Income Tax Return.

faq.q: Are NRIs eligible for the old tax regime deductions?
faq.a: Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) can also opt for the old tax regime and claim eligible deductions and exemptions, provided they meet the criteria for those deductions.

faq.q: What is the maximum deduction under Section 80C?
faq.a: The maximum deduction allowed under Section 80C (including 80CCC and 80CCD(1) for employee's NPS contribution) is ₹1.50 lakhs per financial year.

faq.q: Is HRA exemption available in the new tax regime?
faq.a: No, the HRA exemption is not available under the new tax regime. It is one of the key exemptions unique to the old tax regime.

faq.q: How does home loan interest deduction work in the old regime?
faq.a: Under Section 24(b) of the old regime, you can claim a deduction of up to ₹2 lakhs for interest paid on a home loan for a self-occupied property. For let-out properties, the full interest can be claimed, though the set-off against other income is capped at ₹2 lakhs.
